Demain dans le Portail, on parle et surtout on vit « Cocréation ».

Un sujet exaltant que je triture depuis une vingtaine d’années.

Étudiante en sciences sociales, j’étais passionnée par tout ce qui relevait de l’action collective : qu’est ce qui fait individuellement et collectivement que l’on va dans le mur ou qu’au contraire la dynamique prend un tour inattendu pour aller vers une solution créative et bénéfique ?

Consultante, j’ai animé pendant 10 ans des réunions, des groupes de travail, des séminaires, avec cette même question en tête. Et dans l’ensemble, je ressortais frustrée de mes interventions : j’avais la sensation de rester à un niveau de travail superficiel. De ne pas craquer le code de la Cocréation.

La Cocréation doit pour moi amener à quelque chose de véritablement Nouveau et qui est plus grand que la somme des parties. 
Et à mon sens, pour en arriver là, il y a un travail colossal à mener.

Un travail déjà individuel : comment cocréer si je ne suis pas connecté à ma Source de Création ? Comment cocréer si je n’ai pas conscience de mon Univers Créatif, dans ses aspects métaphysiques et physiques ?

Et un travail collectif, ensuite. Ce travail touche à des questions fascinantes : y-a-t-il des convergences métaphysiques suffisamment proches pour que la Cocréation soit fluide ? Y-a-t-il des complémentarités suffisamment présentes pour expandre le champ des possibles et faire croître l’ensemble des protagonistes à travers l’acte créatif ? Y-a-t-il un désir véritable de cocréer ? Y-a-t-il un cadre qui permette à la Cocréation de se déployer ?

Loin d’être une action mécanique, un assemblage de parties prenantes ou une technique, la Cocréation est pour moi un Art.
Un Art qui requiert une maîtrise de sa Conscience autant qu’une précision chirurgicale.

(Œuvre : Carte d’Oracle « La Cocréation », peinture devant laquelle un ami ingénieur s’est exclamé : « On dirait de l’intrication quantique ». Une chose que j’adore avec mes amis, c’est qu’ils comprennent tout ce que je fais sans que j’ai besoin de le leur expliquer 😆.)

Tecnologie dirompenti, piattaforme digitali e intelligenza artificiale: perché anche le grandi aziende possono perdere il futuro

La storia dell’innovazione tecnologica è piena di paradossi. Molte aziende leader, pur essendo solide, ben gestite e ricche di risorse, non riescono a mantenere la propria posizione quando cambiano le tecnologie, i mercati o i comportamenti dei consumatori. Non falliscono necessariamente perché sono incompetenti o distratte. Spesso accade il contrario: falliscono proprio perché applicano con coerenza le regole del buon management tradizionale. Ascoltano i clienti più importanti, investono nei prodotti più redditizi, migliorano ciò che già funziona e concentrano le risorse dove i margini sono più alti.

L’articolo scientifico di Vincent English, Disruptive Technologies and the Incumbent’s Dilemma in Navigating the Digital and AI Era, riprende la teoria dell’innovazione dirompente formulata da Bower e Christensen e la aggiorna alla luce dell’economia digitale, delle piattaforme e dell’intelligenza artificiale generativa. Il punto centrale è che la “disruption” non è semplicemente una tecnologia nuova o più potente. È un cambiamento che ridefinisce il valore: ciò che all’inizio sembra inferiore, marginale o poco interessante può migliorare rapidamente, conquistare nuovi utenti e infine mettere in crisi gli attori dominanti.

Oggi questo processo è ancora più rapido e complesso. Netflix, Uber, Airbnb, NVIDIA e OpenAI mostrano che la competizione non avviene più soltanto tra prodotti, ma tra ecosistemi, dati, reti di utenti, infrastrutture tecnologiche e modelli di business. Capire l’innovazione dirompente significa quindi comprendere perché il futuro spesso nasce ai margini del mercato, in spazi che le aziende dominanti tendono a sottovalutare.

The Real Meaning of Disruption

Most people get disruption wrong. They think disruption is about breakthrough technology.

It isn’t.

According to Clayton Christensen, disruptive innovations rarely start as better products. They start as simpler, cheaper and more accessible solutions that incumbents dismiss.

Market leaders focus on their best customers. They keep improving performance.

But eventually they deliver more than many customers actually need.

That’s when disruption happens.

New entrants serve overlooked customers or non-consumers. Their products may initially seem inferior. Yet they improve, gain traction and eventually challenge the leaders.

The personal computer wasn’t more powerful than the mainframe.

Netflix wasn’t better than Blockbuster on day one.

The real power of disruption is not superior technology.

It is making products and services accessible to more people.

For innovators, this raises an important question:

Are you making your products better?

Or are you making them accessible to people who cannot use them today?

That is where disruption often begins.

AI is the window right now.

There is no right time. There's only the window — and whether it's still open when you decide to move.

The upgrade is optional. Falling behind isn't.

Seit einigen Monaten nutze ich jede meiner freien Minuten mit KI - begeistert und erschreckt zugleich vom Potential, die diese disruptive Innovation bietet. Wer heute glaubt, sein Berufsbild sei davon nicht betroffen, unterschätzt, was gerade passiert. Für mich als kreativen und innovativen Geist wurde mit KI ein Traum wahr, denn ich kann nun in wenigen Stunden Prototypen und produktive Lösungen entwickeln, wo vorher IT Teams Monate dafür gebraucht hatten - und das für einen Bruchteil der Kosten. So entstand in meiner Freizeit in nur wenigen Monaten ein Portal mit zahlreichen Modulen und integrierten Applikationen. Ein Planungswerkzeug, das eine Unternehmensplanung von der Vision bis zur Umsetzung verbindet. Strategische Boards wie Vision- und Valuestream-Board interagieren mit Operative Board wie Programm- oder Portofolio-Board. Analyse-Board für Planung und Risiko-Management helfen jederzeit das Geschehene aus verschiedenen Perspektiven zu betrachten. Alle miteinander verzahnt. Interagierend mit weiteren Module wie einer Stammdaten-Verwaltung oder einen Rechnungswesen. Ergänzt durch eine Applikation zur Planung von Workshops und Events, die bei der Umsetzung von Projekten unterstützen. Oder einer Flipchart Schmiede, mittels der die für Workshops und Arbeitsgruppen benötigten Flipcharts gestaltet und auf den Plotter ausgedruckt werden können. Wenn man dieses Potential sieht und selber auszureizen vermag, dann kann man nur eine wage Ahnung davon bekommen, wie diese Technologie den Arbeitsmarkt künftig durcheinander wirbeln wird. In weiteren Posts werde ich dich in meine Gedankenwelt mitnehmen und dir zeigen, wie ich versuche normales anders zu denken ...

Denmark: Scandinavian Airlines’ return to India after 17 years suffered a setback when its inaugural Copenhagen-Mumbai flight turned back to Denmark after nearly four hours in the air due to a pending regulatory approval. The Airbus A330-300 reversed course over Azerbaijan and returned to Copenhagen.

SAS said the required authorization had not been issued as expected. Neither the airline nor Indian authorities have disclosed the specific approval that was missing.

The incident disrupted passengers and delayed the launch of SAS’s new Mumbai route, which was planned to operate five times weekly as part of the carrier’s expansion into the Indian market.

🚨 THE BIGGEST PROBLEM IN THE WORLD ISN'T WHAT YOU THINK IT IS. 🚨

Most people think our biggest problems are inflation, debt, corruption, poverty, housing, healthcare, climate change, political division, or economic instability.

They're wrong.

Those are symptoms.

The real problem is that humanity is operating on disconnected systems.

Our financial systems don't communicate efficiently.
Our governments don't coordinate effectively.
Our institutions optimize for separate goals.
Our currencies compete instead of connecting.
Our data exists in silos.
Our incentives are fragmented.

Every day, trillions of dollars move through layers of friction, intermediaries, delays, fees, incompatible systems, and outdated infrastructure.

We have connected the entire world through the internet.

Yet we still haven't truly connected the systems that move value.

Think about that.

A message can travel across the globe in milliseconds.

Money often cannot.

The result?

Lost productivity.
Lost opportunity.
Lost trust.
Lost potential.

Humanity isn't suffering from a lack of resources.

We're suffering from a lack of interoperability.

The next great revolution won't be another app.

It won't be another social network.

It won't even be another currency.

The next revolution will come from connecting what is currently disconnected.

That is the vision behind GLIX.

Not a replacement for existing systems.

A bridge between them.

A Universal Money Bridge designed to help connect currencies, payment networks, institutions, businesses, technologies, and people into a more efficient global financial ecosystem.

Because history wasn't changed by those who built the biggest walls.

It was changed by those who built the most important bridges.

The future belongs to connection.

The future belongs to interoperability.

The future belongs to systems that work together instead of against each other.

The question is:

Will we keep patching a fragmented world... 

Or will we finally start connecting it?

Post-separation abuse doesn’t always look like what people expect.

Sometimes it’s:
• The missing school uniform
• The withheld passport
• The last-minute cancellation
• The constant changes to arrangements
• Being left out of important information
• Having to repeatedly explain yourself to schools, professionals and family members

Taken individually, these incidents can seem small.

But when they happen repeatedly, they can create confusion, instability and ongoing control long after the relationship has ended.

Many parents experiencing post-separation abuse spend years questioning themselves because each incident is dismissed as a misunderstanding, coincidence or mistake.

C’est lui qui m’a appris que gouverner un territoire, c’est d’abord oser regarder là où les autres ne regardent pas encore.

En 1996, il faisait d’Issy-les-Moulineaux la première ville française à se doter d’un site internet municipal ￼ — quand la plupart des élus ne savaient même pas ce qu’était le web. Ce n’était pas de la technologie pour la technologie. C’était une vision : utiliser le numérique pour moderniser la relation entre la collectivité et ses habitants, et anticiper les effets de la révolution numérique sur les usages comme sur l’action publique. ￼

C’est cette philosophie que j’ai tenté de transposer dans ma propre ville : ne pas attendre que les transformations arrivent, les provoquer. Accepter la sérendipité comme méthode. Embrasser le disruptif comme boussole.

Il aimait à dire que “le fait qu’il y ait de moins en moins d’argent public contraint à de plus en plus d’imagination, d’ouverture d’esprit, de recherche de mutualisation.” ￼ Ces mots résonnent encore aujourd’hui dans chaque projet que je porte pour mon territoire.

Sous son impulsion, Issy-les-Moulineaux est devenu un pôle numérique de référence en France et à l’international ￼ — preuve qu’un élu local déterminé peut changer l’échelle d’une ville et en faire un modèle pour d’autres.

Merci, André, pour m’avoir montré que l’audace n’est pas un luxe réservé aux grandes métropoles.
Que le courage de l’innovation est un devoir d’élu.
Et que la sérendipité se cultive — pour peu qu’on ait l’humilité de rester en éveil.

Repose en paix, bâtisseur.

Because digital photography threatened everything that made Kodak successful:

💰 Film rolls
💰 Photo printing
💰 The entire photography ecosystem

Kodak faced a difficult choice:

Protect the profits of today...
or build the future of tomorrow.

That's the hidden danger of success.

Sometimes innovation isn't your biggest challenge.

The real challenge is being willing to disrupt your own business before someone else does.

Because markets don't reward who invented the future.

They reward who adapts to it.

It's about every founder, startup, entrepreneur, and business leader facing change today.

Education.
Retail.
Media.

Are you building for the next decade...

The companies that survive aren't always the biggest.

1. "Pseudo Harmony" (Budaya Asal Bos Senang)
Definisi: Ketenangan semu organisasi yang dibangun di atas pembungkaman pendapat, ego sektoral, dan ketakutan staf menyuarakan kebenaran.
Indikator: Kritik dianggap tidak loyal, muncul "raja kecil" di unit kerja, dan laporan performa selalu disajikan manis tanpa dinamika.
Dampak: Hilangnya mekanisme koreksi mandiri, stagnasi inovasi total, serta rapat hanya menjadi formalitas tanpa solusi.
Konklusi: Organisasi hancur saat kompetensi dikalahkan oleh ego struktural dan inovasi dianggap sebagai ancaman politis.

2. Dampak Pemangku Kepentingan
Pasien: Bingung karena info antar-unit bertolak belakang; lelah menghadapi petugas kaku dan masalah lama yang terus dibiarkan.
Staf: Memilih masa bodoh demi menggugurkan kewajiban karena tahu siapa yang bicara lebih penting daripada bobot ide.
Manajerial: Terjebak delusi rapat yang tenang, menerima laporan bagus di atas kertas namun bingung operasional lapangan stagnan.

3. Solusi Strategis: "Reliability Culture" (Prinsip HRO)
Prinsip: Budaya keandalan dibentuk bukan untuk memaksa kepatuhan buta, melainkan membangun sistem yang bersih, jelas, dan sesuai realita.
Karakteristik: Meritokrasi berbasis kepakaran, diskusi faktual, serta menjadikan staf lini depan sebagai radar dinamika operasional.
Fokus: Dobrak praktik kolegisme dan patronase birokrasi, lalu ganti dengan ekosistem pembelajaran High Reliability Organization (HRO).

Kesimpulan Implikatif: Ubah paradigma kepemimpinan dari "siapa yang bicara" menjadi "apa bobot pernyataannya." Memelihara harmoni palsu hanya akan melumpuhkan deteksi kerusakan sistemik. Tumbuhkan Reliability Culture agar kebijakan manajemen menjadi realistis dan relevan dengan lapangan.

Der Wendepunkt kam nicht durch bessere Produkte.
Nicht durch eine Markenoffensive.
Und nicht durch externes Kapital.
Was entschied: eine Frage, die Kodak nie gestellt hat.

CEO Shigetaka Komori machte 2000 keine Panikentscheidung.
Er machte eine Inventur.

Nicht: In welchen neuen Markt gehen wir?
Sondern: Was wissen wir, das niemand anderes hat?

Antwort: 45.000 Materialtechnologien aus 60 Jahren Filmforschung.

Kollagen, der Hauptbestandteil von Fotoemulsionen, ist chemisch identisch mit dem Wirkstoff in Antiaging-Kosmetik. Das wurde zu Astalift.
TAC-Folie, ursprünglich Schutzschicht für Fotofilme, ist der kritische Bestandteil in LCD-Display-Polarisatoren. Marktanteil heute: über 70 %.
Chemische Verbindungen aus der Filmentwicklung wurden direkt in pharmazeutische Bildgebung und Diagnostik übertragen.

Das ist der Punkt, den viele übersehen:

Diversifikation ohne Inventur ist Kapitalvernichtung.
Fujifilm hat keine neuen Märkte gesucht.
Es hat den eigenen technologischen Kern in neue Märkte übersetzt.

Fujifilm verschob sich von:

Fotochemie zu pharmazeutischer Wirkstoffforschung
Filmschutztechnologie zu LCD-Infrastruktur
Produktverteidigung zu Plattformstrategie
Reaktion auf Marktdruck zu struktureller Destillation

Und genau hier scheitern die meisten Unternehmen in der Krise:

Sie fragen, welche neuen Märkte sie betreten sollen.
Sie fragen nicht, welchen Kern sie bereits besitzen.

Kodak hatte dieselbe Technologiebasis wie Fujifilm.
Es fehlte nicht die Ressource. Es fehlte die Frage.

In Dallas erschien die Zukunft nicht als Bedrohung, sondern als unbequeme Position in einer Gewinnrechnung.

Blockbusters Verzicht auf den Kauf von Netflix zeigt, wie Rentabilitätskennzahlen zur institutionellen Verteidigung gegen strategische Erneuerung werden können.

Im September 2000 trat Netflix in Dallas nicht als globaler Streamingkonzern auf, sondern als verlustträchtige Internetfirma nach dem Platzen der Dotcom-Euphorie. Das Angebot war nüchtern: Blockbuster sollte Netflix für 50 Mio. USD kaufen; Reed Hastings, Marc Randolph und Barry McCarthy wollten das Onlinegeschäft aufbauen. Die Episode wird oft als arroganter Irrtum erzählt. Diese Lesart ist eingängig, aber zu flach.

Der eigentliche Konflikt lag weniger in einem fehlenden Blick für das Internet als in einer Erfolgslogik, die den bestehenden Gewinn schützte. Blockbuster meldete 2004 rund 9.100 Filialen und 6,1 Mrd. USD Umsatz. Gleichzeitig waren verspätete Rückgaben ein relevanter Ergebnisbaustein: Blockbuster hatte für 2005 den direkten Effekt entfallender Säumnisgebühren auf 400 bis 450 Mio. USD Umsatz und 250 bis 300 Mio. USD operatives Ergebnis geschätzt.

Damit wurde Netflix nicht nur als kleines, defizitäres Unternehmen bewertet. Es bedrohte eine interne Architektur aus Filialnetzen, Mietverträgen, Personal, Inventar, operativen Kennzahlen und Kundengewohnheiten. Jede digitale Beschleunigung hätte zunächst Kennzahlen belastet, an denen Blockbusters Stärke gemessen wurde.

Das ist die institutionelle Falle reifer Unternehmen. Sie erkennen Disruption oft früher, als spätere Legenden behaupten. Doch wenn Kapitalmarkt, Management und operative Organisation auf den Schutz des aktuellen Margenprofils kalibriert sind, erscheint eine Zukunftsinvestition wie Selbstbeschädigung.

In 1999, Marc Benioff walked into the enterprise software world and effectively declared war on a multi-billion-dollar industry standard.
At the time, conventional wisdom was absolute: software had to be expensive, required months of tedious installation, and lived strictly behind a company’s firewall.
Benioff’s radical proposition? CRM should be delivered entirely as Software as a Service (SaaS).
The incumbents laughed. Analysts dismissed it. Investors hesitated.
But that is the burden of the forerunner. When you are the first to cross into uncharted territory, you don't find a paved road, you find intense resistance.
The Blueprint for Disruptive Leadership
What separates iconic leaders from the rest isn't just a good idea; it's the stamina to defend it. Innovation and grit are two sides of the same coin. To scale a radical concept, you must be willing to endure the discomfort of being misunderstood and/or disliked for a very long time.
You can present data and you can build a flawless business case. But without the raw courage to propose an uncomfortable idea and the grit to see it through, your vision will die in a conference room.
The DNA of an Industry Pathfinder
Being an industry pathfinder requires a rare mix of courage, grit, and absolute conviction. Pathfinders don’t wait for permission or validation from the market. They challenge the status quo because they possess the foresight to see a better way long before anyone else can even imagine it.
By standing firm against the critics, Benioff didn't just build Salesforce, he cleared the path for an entire generation of businesses. That single, defiant proposition birthed the trillion-dollar cloud revolution.
•	What radical proposition are you sitting on today because it feels too risky?
•	Are you ready to stop managing the current reality and start pathfinding the future?
Don't wait for a map. Be the forerunner. Forge the path.

The universe isn't empty space with a few galaxies floating around. It has a skeleton.

NASA's James Webb Space Telescope just gave us the clearest look at it ever — a map of the Cosmic Web: the vast network of dark matter filaments and gas that connects every galaxy in existence.

The numbers are hard to process: 164,000 galaxies. 13.7 billion years of history. One image.

The team behind it — led by PhD student Hossein Hatamnia and Professor Bahram Mobasher at UC Riverside — used COSMOS-Web, the largest survey ever conducted by JWST, covering a patch of sky three times the size of a full Moon. 

Their infrared instruments detected galaxies invisible to any previous telescope, tracing the web all the way back to when the universe was just one billion years old.

And here's what makes this genuinely mind-bending: this structure has always been there. We've been living inside it for 13.7 billion years. We just didn't have the tools to see it.
Until now.

Et puis, au bout de quelques années, j’ai abdiqué. 
Je suis devenue un Maître en Franglais. 
Le point confortable ? Je faisais partie intégrante de la tribu.
Le prix à payer ? Je me suis éloignée encore plus de mon véritable langage.

Retrouver les mots qui peuplent mon Monde fait partie du chemin que j’ai parcouru ces dernières années.
Un chemin qui a supposé - et je pèse mes mots - de me désintoxiquer. Tout mon Être était pollué de termes et de tournures de phrases qui n’avaient absolument rien à voir avec moi. Et qui me donnaient, si j’y étais véritablement attentive, une sensation de sang dans le bouche et de contraction dans les tripes, assortie d’une vague envie de mourir.

Au cours de ce processus de désintoxication, le Franglais est bien évidemment parti. 
En m’en séparant je me suis rendue compte de deux choses : il me donnait la sensation d’être cool, de faire partie de cet univers mondialisé à la pointe de la modernité. Formulé autrement : il me narcissisait. Et il me permettait de vivre en mode robot, au lieu de plonger dans mes profondeurs et de les ramener à la surface pour enfin m’exprimer telle que j’étais.

J’ai dû accepter ce qui me semblait inacceptable : mon style romanesque, conceptuel, ésotérique, poétique. Ce style à 1 000 lieues de la communication business et qui soulevait chez mon Humain Normé Terrifié des montagnes de peur et de honte. 

Mais, en acceptant cet inacceptable a priori, j’ai retrouvé ce qui est porteur d’une valeur infinie : j’ai retrouvé la puissance de mon Verbe Créateur. J’ai retrouvé la Vie.

The thing that almost broke you might be exactly what positions you to serve at the highest level.

Your disruption isn't your liability, it's your blueprint. The crisis that forced you to rebuild, the loss that made you question everything, the health scare that stopped you cold, that's not the thing you hide from clients. That's often the exact experience that creates your most premium offer.

Here's what I've learned through kidney failure, transplant, cancer, and stroke: The entrepreneurs creating the highest value offers aren't the ones who never failed. They're the ones who went through something, separated what actually happened from the story they decided it meant, and built their expertise from that ground.

Your worst disruption taught you something no business school could. It forced you to develop capacities most people never need. It gave you a perspective that only exists on the other side of what you survived.

The problem isn't that you went through something difficult. The problem is the story you're telling yourself about what that means about you, your worthiness, your ability to serve others.

When you clear the story underneath, you don't just heal from the disruption. You discover the disruption was preparing you for the work you're actually here to do.

Something underneath is running you, and you can't name it. But once you can, everything changes.

Saya membaca kenyataan MB Johor bahawa DAP tidak pernah & tidak akan ada dalam Kerajaan Johor BN.
Terus terang, kenyataan ini menimbulkan lebih banyak persoalan daripada jawapan.
Jika benar ini soal prinsip, mengapa prinsip yang sama tidak digunakan di Putrajaya?
Selepas PRU15, UMNO & BN bukan sahaja bekerjasama dengan DAP, malah bersama-sama membentuk Kerajaan Persekutuan. Menteri UMNO duduk semeja dengan menteri DAP setiap minggu dalam Kabinet. Mereka mempertahankan kerajaan yang sama, meluluskan bajet yang sama & berkongsi tanggungjawab yang sama.
Jadi apabila tiba musim pilihan raya Johor, tiba-tiba DAP dijadikan isu semula.
Yang berubah sebenarnya DAP atau pendirian UMNO?
Rakyat Johor bukan budak-budak yang boleh diperdaya dengan naratif yang berubah mengikut musim politik. Hari ini kawan di Putrajaya, esok musuh di Johor. Hari ini kerjasama demi kestabilan negara, esok kononnya demi prinsip negeri.
Lebih menarik apabila disebut "Bangsa Johor".
Bangsa Johor sepatutnya membawa maksud seluruh rakyat Johor tanpa mengira kaum, agama atau parti politik. Ia tidak seharusnya dijadikan slogan politik untuk menakut-nakutkan rakyat terhadap pihak tertentu apabila pilihan raya semakin hampir.
Hakikatnya rakyat semakin letih dengan politik lama.
- BN menyalahkan PH.
- PH menyalahkan PN.
- PN menyalahkan BN.
Tetapi kos sara hidup terus meningkat, harga rumah semakin sukar dimiliki generasi muda, peluang pekerjaan berkualiti masih menjadi cabaran & ramai anak Johor terus berhijrah mencari masa depan yang lebih baik.
Jangan terlalu yakin dengan mandat semalam sehingga terlupa membaca sentimen hari ini.
UMNO pernah menganggap Johor sebagai kubu yang tidak boleh ditembusi. Banyak parti dalam sejarah politik Malaysia juga pernah beranggapan mereka tidak boleh dikalahkan.
Rakyat akhirnya membuktikan sebaliknya.
Tiada parti mempunyai hak mutlak ke atas undi rakyat. Mandat bukan hak milik mana-mana parti. Ia dipinjam oleh rakyat & boleh ditarik balik pada bila-bila masa.
Jika percanggahan pendirian, retorik pilihan raya & politik lama terus dimainkan, jangan terkejut jika BN menerima kejutan yang tidak dijangka dalam PRN Johor 2026.
Kerana pada akhirnya, rakyat tidak makan slogan.
Rakyat mahu hasil.
Jika rakyat merasakan tiada lagi perbezaan antara BN, PH & PN, jangan terkejut jika mereka mula mencari alternatif baharu yang benar-benar meletakkan rakyat mengatasi kepentingan parti.

Thailand Among Economies Facing Proposed 12.5% U.S. Tariff Over Forced-Labor Concerns

Thailand is among 54 economies facing a proposed 12.5% U.S. tariff under a new trade measure announced by President Donald Trump's administration over what Washington says is a failure to adequately prevent imports produced with forced labor from entering their markets.

The proposal by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) stems from a Section 301 investigation into forced labor and unfair trade practices. The USTR said Thailand and other affected economies had failed to effectively establish or enforce measures banning imports made with forced labor.

Thailand joins China, Vietnam, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, India, Australia, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and dozens of other economies in the 12.5% tariff category. Canada, Ecuador, the European Union, Indonesia, Mexico and Pakistan would face a lower 10% tariff. 

The proposal is part of the Trump administration's effort to rebuild tariff measures after the U.S. Supreme Court in February struck down tariffs imposed under emergency economic powers. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said major trading partners had failed to address imports linked to forced labor, creating unfair competition for American workers. 

The USTR is also considering a mechanism that would allow limited quantities of textile and apparel imports to enter the United States at reduced tariff rates. Products exempt from the proposed tariffs include energy products, certain rare earth minerals and metals, beef, coffee, selected fruits and vegetables, pharmaceuticals, organic chemicals and aircraft parts.

The establishment of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) marks a pivotal shift in Southeast Asian economic integration. By pairing Johor’s land availability and manufacturing capacity with Singapore’s global financial muscle, the zone has created a high-velocity business corridor. However, as thousands of companies, data centers, and advanced manufacturing plants expand across this border, they face an unexpected roadblock: the frictional cost of moving capital.

While physical cross-border travel is being streamlined through passport-free QR immigration trials, the financial rails behind them remain bogged down by legacy legacy architectures. To unlock the full potential of the JS-SEZ, the region needs a parallel leap forward in payment infrastructure: on-chain cross-border stablecoin settlement.

Why Stablecoins Fit the Special Economic Zone? 

Stablecoins, cryptographic tokens pegged 1:1 to fiat currencies like USD, SGD, or MYR, offer a  programmable, internet-native alternative to traditional banking rails. Within an economic zone like the JS-SEZ, they serve as a digital ledger that bridges two distinct regulatory jurisdictions.

Instead of waiting for multiple clearinghouses to reconcile ledgers, stablecoins utilize public or permissioned blockchains to achieve atomic settlement. Money moves from a Singaporean parent company’s wallet to a Johor subsidiary’s wallet in under three seconds, operating 24/7/365. This accelerates supply chain velocity, allowing cargo clearance and supplier payments to happen simultaneously.

By passing directly from sender to receiver, stablecoins eliminate the chain of correspondent banks. For manufacturing components moving between Singapore and Johor, a company can settle a multi-million dollar invoice for fractions of a cent in network gas fees, drastically reducing operational overhead.

Using smart contracts, payments within the SEZ can be tied directly to physical milestones. For instance, a stablecoin payment can be locked in a digital escrow and automatically released to a Malaysian logistics provider the exact moment a digitised cargo clearance sensor registers that the delivery truck has crossed the Second Link

The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone represents the future of ASEAN’s industrial and digital economy. However, a 21st-century economic zone cannot run efficiently on 20th-century financial rails.

By legalizing and structuring regulated stablecoin settlement flows through compliance hubs like Labuan, Malaysia can offer international investors an unmatched operational ecosystem. The first movers to bridge the physical connectivity of the economic zone with the digital speed of programmable asset settlement will ultimately set the standard for cross-border commerce across the region.

Tangannya gemetar saat membuka kotak beludru biru berisi medali emas penghargaan dunia penerbangan sipil. Baginya, medali itu bukan sekadar simbol prestasi pribadi, melainkan bukti bahwa Indonesia pernah berdiri sejajar dengan raksasa aviasi dunia. Di balik sorot matanya, ada luka panjang tentang sebuah negeri yang nyaris berhasil terbang tinggi—lalu dipaksa jatuh sebelum menembus awan.

Ketika Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara lahir pada 1976, Habibie memulainya hanya dengan 20 orang. Dua dekade kemudian, perusahaan itu menjelma menjadi simbol kebangkitan teknologi nasional dengan 48 ribu pekerja dan mimpi besar bernama N-250 Gatotkaca. 

Pesawat itu bukan proyek kaleng-kaleng. Ia adalah kebanggaan Asia: pesawat turboprop pertama di kelasnya yang memakai teknologi fly by wire, sistem komputerisasi canggih yang saat itu bahkan belum lazim dipakai banyak negara. Saat N-250 mengudara di Bandung tahun 1996, dunia terpukau. Indonesia seperti sedang menulis takdir baru: dari negara pengimpor teknologi menjadi pencipta teknologi.

Tapi sejarah kadang tak ramah kepada mereka yang terlalu visioner. Krisis moneter 1998 datang bersama syarat-syarat dari International Monetary Fund. Salah satu klausul itu  adalah penghentian subsidi untuk IPTN. 

Artinya sederhana tapi tragis: proyek N-250 harus berhenti, meski tinggal selangkah menuju sertifikasi internasional. Habibie melihat semua yang dibangunnya perlahan dihancurkan atas nama penyelamatan ekonomi. Ironisnya, bertahun-tahun kemudian, maskapai-maskapai Indonesia justru membeli pesawat asing dengan spesifikasi mirip rancangan anak bangsa. Habibie menyaksikan negeri ini mengimpor mimpi yang dulu pernah berhasil mereka ciptakan sendiri.

$XFAB X-FAB Silicon Foundries is the only large independent specialty semiconductor foundry in Europe. 

It does not make AI chips. It does not make memory. It makes the analog and mixed-signal chips that go inside every modern car, every industrial robot, every medical implant, and every power conversion system in the energy transition. 
Six fabs across Germany, France, Malaysia and the United States. 
4,500 employees. 
$870M in 2025 revenues. 
And the single most strategically important semiconductor company Europe has and barely knows it. 

What a specialty foundry actually does, because it is different from everything TSMC does

TSMC makes cutting-edge digital logic chips at 3nm and 5nm. That is not what the world runs on day to day. The chips inside a car power steering module, a pacemaker, a solar inverter, a factory sensor, or an EV battery management system require analog precision, high voltage tolerance and long product lifetimes, not raw transistor density. These chips are built on mature nodes from 180nm down to 110nm and are manufactured by specialty foundries like X-FAB.
The key economics: once a customer designs a chip using X-FAB's process and it enters production, the average product lifetime exceeds 12 years. X-FAB earns a recurring manufacturing fee per wafer for over a decade on each design win. A modern high-end electric vehicle contains up to 180 X-FAB manufactured chips.

The 2025 numbers and 2026 trajectory

FY2025 revenue: 
- $870M, up 6.6% year on year. 
- Q4 2025 alone: $222M, up 18% year on year. The recovery from the automotive and industrial inventory correction is underway.
- Q1 2026: $196M, down 4% year on year on a soft seasonal quarter, but Q1 2026 EBITDA margin of 17.5% and EPS of $0.01 beat the consensus of -$0.01 by 149%. The underlying profitability is recovering faster than revenue.
- Q2 2026 guidance: $190-200M with EBITDA margin of 17-20%. Management confirmed steady recovery trajectory.

The $1 billion capacity expansion is the core of the thesis

Between 2023 and 2025, X-FAB committed $1.0 billion in new capacity across all six fabs. 
This adds approximately 49,000 wafer starts per month to total capacity. The original target was $1.5 billion in annual revenue by 2026. 
The more realistic timeline, given the automotive cycle slowdown, is 2027-2028. But the capacity is being built. The demand is coming. 
And at $1.5 billion in revenue with a 33% EBITDA margin, the company generates $500 million in annual EBITDA versus an enterprise value today of approximately $1.4 billion. 
That is an EV/EBITDA of roughly 2.8x on target economics. 

The European Chips Act is the strategic underwriter

The EU Chips Act deploys €43 billion to rebuild European semiconductor sovereignty. X-FAB's Corbeil-Essonnes fab in France is one of the primary beneficiaries. 
The French government's France 2030 plan and EU sovereign semiconductor strategy explicitly require an independent European specialty foundry at scale. 
X-FAB is the only one that qualifies. Government co-investment, subsidized financing, and strategic support for the French fab expansion are reducing the effective cost and risk of the investment cycle significantly. 
The EU is not funding X-FAB out of charity. It is funding it because without X-FAB, there is no European semiconductor sovereignty in analog and mixed-signal.

The Melexis anchor gives revenue certainty

Melexis, the Belgian automotive chip maker, is X-FAB's largest customer at approximately 35-40% of revenue. Melexis has signed long-term agreements for 2023-2025 at 350nm and 180nm, and a separate LTA for 2024-2027 at 110nm. 
To secure capacity, Melexis prepaid €189 million in advance purchase commitments. Melexis also built its own assembly facility adjacent to X-FAB's Kuching, Malaysia fab to reduce logistics costs. 
This is not a customer relationship. This is a structural interdependency that provides multi-year revenue visibility.

The photonics door is now open

- December 4, 2025: X-FAB and LIGENTEC announced an expanded collaboration on integrated photonics. The partnership specifically brings X-FAB's XPH90 Silicon Photonics (SOI) process and Thin Film Lithium Niobate technology to market jointly. 
Lithium niobate is the next frontier for ultra-high-speed optical modulators, enabling data rates beyond what standard silicon photonics can achieve. 
This puts X-FAB directly inside the AI data center optical interconnect supply chain, alongside the other names in this thesis: $IQE, $SOI, $SIVE.

- December 5, 2025: X-FAB launched XbloX, a design acceleration platform specifically for SiC MOSFETs, enabling power chip designers to bring silicon carbide transistors to market faster using X-FAB's established SiC processes. Expands the SiC customer pipeline beyond existing Tier 1 relationships.

The SiC growth engine is the next re-rating catalyst

SiC revenues in 2025 were approximately $80M. Only 25% of fully electric vehicles currently use SiC inverters, expected to double by 2035. 
X-FAB's Lubbock, Texas fab is the US SiC production center, benefiting from the US CHIPS Act in addition to the EU Chips Act on the European side. STMicroelectronics is investing €5 billion in a new SiC facility in Italy. Onsemi is investing $2 billion in Czech Republic for SiC. The SiC ecosystem is being built at scale. X-FAB is the only independent foundry serving it without captive conflict.
 
The valuation vs peers (EV/Sales)

- X-FAB : 1.5x
- GlobalFoundries : 2.5x
- $TSMC : 8x
X-FAB trades at the steepest discount in the specialty foundry universe despite being the only pure-play European specialty foundry with explicit government support. 

Risks deserve honesty

Net debt will reach approximately $330M by end 2026 as the investment cycle peaks. 
Free cash flow is negative during the capex phase. 
The automotive cycle is still recovering, with Q1 2026 revenue down 4% year on year. 
SiC ramp is running behind the original ambitious schedule. 
Melexis concentration at 35-40% remains a structural risk despite LTA protection. 
Currency risk: revenues predominantly in USD, costs partly in EUR. 

The setup if the thesis is right

$870M revenue growing toward $1.5B. 
$1B in new capacity already committed and partially built. EU Chips Act backing as strategic European semiconductor asset. 
SiC ramp from $80M. 
Photonics door open through LIGENTEC. 
US CHIPS Act benefits on the SiC side. 
$500M in EBITDA on target economics versus $1.4B EV today. 

The market is pricing the investment cycle and the automotive downturn. It is not pricing what comes out the other side.

Not financial advice. Do your own due diligence.

Seperti yang OOMF tahu, sudah rutinitasku ngomong di stream, dan isi kontenku kadang kritik ini itu. Termasuk kemarin, aku ngomongin rupiah yang tembus 18.000 per dolar, bareng sama beberapa vtuber lain.

Lalu ada tweet yang singgah di timeline.
Katanya, penyebab rupiah ambruk adalah kaum nyinyir yang tiap hari ngeributin pemerintah di sosmed. Konon, postingan sosmed kita memberikan efek buruk ke IDR.

Aku sampai baca ulang beberapa kali, nahan ketawa karena benar-benar gak habis pikir.

Bukan sekadar salah, ini argumen yang berbahaya.

Rupiah Digerakkan oleh Siapa?

Kalau kamu pernah main atau nonton orang stream game strategy, kamu mungkin familiar konsep supply and demand. 

Harga barang naik kalau banyak yang mau beli, turun kalau banyak yang mau jual. Nilai tukar rupiah bekerja persis seperti itu di pasar valas atau pasar uang internasional.

Yang jual-beli rupiah di pasar ini bukan kamu. Bukan aku. Bukan OOMF yang nge-quote tweet berita pemerintah dengan emoji nangis, emoji batu, atau emoji badut tiap pagi. Kalaupun kita jual-beli valas, retail kayak kita tuh cuma remah-remah.

Yang ngegerakin kurs adalah bank sentral, hedge fund raksasa, perusahaan multinasional, dan investor institusional yang kelola dana triliunan dolar.

Mereka ambil keputusan berdasarkan data: pertumbuhan ekonomi, inflasi, suku bunga, neraca perdagangan, dan stabilitas politik. Mereka tidak scroll Twitter sambil buka Bloomberg.

Jadi pertanyaannya sederhana: apakah postingan netizen Indonesia punya bobot yang cukup untuk ngegerakin pasar valas global? Jawaban singkatnya: tidak.

Data yang ada bukan rahasia. Surplus neraca perdagangan Indonesia turun hampir 50% dalam setahun terakhir. Cadangan devisa turun ke level terendah hampir dua tahun karena Bank Indonesia harus jor-joran intervensi pasar.

IHSG terkoreksi lebih dari 33% sejak awal tahun. Modal asing keluar dari pasar keuangan Indonesia dalam jumlah signifikan.

Semua ini terjadi karena kombinasi faktor eksternal seperti ketidakpastian geopolitik dan penguatan dolar AS global, serta faktor internal berupa fundamental ekonomi yang melemah. Faktor-faktor ini yang dibaca oleh investor institusional, dan membuat mereka memilih memindahkan modalnya ke tempat lain.

Tapi Bukankah Sentimen Bisa Pengaruhi Pasar?

Ya, sentimen pasar memang nyata dan mempengaruhi pergerakan kurs. Tapi sentimen yang dimaksud adalah sentimen pelaku pasar keuangan global, bukan sentimen yang terbentuk dari timeline Twitter. Mereka membaca laporan ekonomi, proyeksi IMF, dan keputusan kebijakan pemerintah. Bukan thread panjang dari akun anonim.

Dan kalau pun kita terima premis bahwa suasana negatif di publik bisa melemahkan kepercayaan investor, pertanyaannya jadi: apa yang menciptakan suasana negatif itu? Kondisi ekonominya. Bukan kritiknya.

Analoginya begini: kalau ada asap di dapur, yang salah bukan orang yang berteriak ada asap. Yang salah adalah sumber apinya. Menyalahkan yang berteriak bukan solusi. Itu hanya cara supaya dapur tetap terbakar tanpa ada yang ribut.

Negara-negara yang pernah bangkrut akibat krisis ekonomi seperti Argentina, Venezuela, atau Sri Lanka, tidak bangkrut karena warganya terlalu banyak ngomong di sosmed. Mereka bangkrut karena mismanajemen kebijakan yang tidak dikritisi sejak dini, karena alarm diabaikan, serta karena suara peringatan ditekan atau dianggap provokasi.

Kritik bukan racun demokrasi. Kritik adalah sistem peringatan dini.

Menyalahkan orang yang mempertanyakan kebijakan atas akibat dari kebijakan itu sendiri adalah logika yang justru membahayakan.

Aku tidak tahu apakah tweet itu ditulis dengan niat buruk atau cuma frustrasi yang salah arah. Tapi argumennya tetap keliru, serta tanpa data yang mendukung. 

Lebih baik kita fokus membicarakan, apa yang seharusnya dilakukan pemerintah, serta apa yang seharusnya kita lakukan dalam menghadapi semua ini.

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)
Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

I had the pleasure of receiving a courtesy call from H.E. Hayrullo Khayitbayevich Bazarov, Governor of the Fergana Region of Uzbekistan, who is currently on an official visit to Malaysia, accompanied by H.E. Dr. Karomidin Gadoev, Ambassador of Uzbekistan to Malaysia.

Fergana is one of Uzbekistan’s most developed industrial and economic regions, with strong capabilities in agriculture, manufacturing, logistics, and a rapidly growing industrial base. Our discussion focused on building a practical and mutually beneficial partnership between Selangor and the Fergana Region, moving beyond traditional country-to-country engagements towards stronger state-to-state cooperation.

I shared Selangor’s strengths as Malaysia’s leading economic powerhouse, including our high-technology manufacturing sector, semiconductor ecosystem, halal industry, aerospace capabilities, life sciences, data centres and digital economy. We explored opportunities for collaboration in research and development, particularly in technology-driven industries where both regions can leverage their respective strengths.

Food security and agro-industrial cooperation were also key areas of discussion. Fergana expressed its interest in expanding agricultural exports to Malaysia and highlighted ongoing efforts to improve logistics connectivity between Central Asia and Southeast Asia. We exchanged views on how transportation and supply chain challenges can be addressed to facilitate greater trade and investment flows between our regions.

The meeting also touched on water management and environmental sustainability. Given Selangor’s experience in water governance and infrastructure development, I welcomed the opportunity for technical exchanges and knowledge-sharing, including potential collaboration involving Air Selangor’s expertise.

I also welcomed Fergana’s proposal for closer institutional cooperation, including the possibility of a Memorandum of Understanding between Selangor and the Fergana Region. Both sides agreed to continue discussions and facilitate reciprocal visits by government agencies and industry representatives in the coming months to identify concrete areas of collaboration.

As the key driver of Malaysia’s economy, Selangor remains committed to building strategic partnerships with regions and countries that share our aspirations for sustainable growth, innovation and shared prosperity.

I was also honoured to be presented with a doppi (traditional Uzbek skullcap) and a chopon (traditional embroidered coat), both of which hold deep cultural significance in Uzbekistan. I am grateful for this thoughtful gesture and privileged to don these symbols of Uzbekistan’s rich heritage and traditions.

I look forward to strengthening ties between Selangor and the Fergana Region and translating today’s discussions into meaningful partnerships that will benefit the people and businesses of both regions.

A woman accused her husband of stealing ₦12 million from their joint account.

The entire family turned against him almost immediately.

Even his own mother called him a disgrace 😭 💔

The money had disappeared overnight. And somehow, all fingers pointed at him.

Within days, people stopped asking questions. They had already decided he was guilty.

His wife cried everywhere. At church. At family meetings. Even on social media.

People praised her for staying calm through such a painful betrayal.

Meanwhile, her husband watched his reputation collapse.

Friends stopped calling. Relatives stopped visiting. People who had known him for years suddenly looked at him differently.

The pressure became unbearable. Eventually, he moved out.

For seven months, he lived alone.

Seven months of whispers. Seven months of judgment. Seven months of being treated like a thief.

And through it all, nobody stood by him. Not even his own children.

Then something happened.

The bank contacted both of them. There were irregularities in account records and investigators wanted statements.

At first, nobody seemed worried.

The case looked simple. Missing money. One obvious suspect.

But as investigators dug deeper, small details stopped making sense.

Transaction records didn't match earlier claims. Dates didn't line up. Certain transfers raised new questions. Question nobody had been asking.

For the first time in 7 months, attention shifted away from the husband.

Then the truth came out. The ₦12 million had never been stolen.

The husband had never touched a kobo of it. The money had been transferred by someone with full access to the account.

Someone nobody had suspected.

His wife. She had secretly moved the money months earlier.

Not to another man. Not to a business. But to her younger brother.

The same brother she always claimed was struggling financially.

He had used the money for sports betting. And lost almost all of it.

When the truth came out, the entire family was stunned.

The woman who had spent months accusing her husband was the one responsible for the missing money.

She later admitted she never intended for things to get out of control.

She believed her brother would win the money back.

She believed she could quietly replace the funds before anyone noticed. But when everything went wrong, panic took over.

One lie became another. Then another. Until an innocent man lost his home, his reputation, and the trust of his own children.

Eventually, he forgave her. At least publicly. But he never moved back into the house.

When family members asked why, he gave an answer that nobody forgot, "You can recover money, but you can't recover trust."

The marriage survived on paper. But many people believed it ended the day the accusation was made.

The money wasn't what destroyed the marriage. It was the fact that an innocent man was abandoned by the people who were supposed to know him best.

If your spouse falsely accused you of stealing ₦12 million and the entire family turned against you for seven months, could you ever truly move on after the truth came out?

Would you stay, leave, or forgive but never trust again? Tell me honestly.

Pig farmers in the central state of Selangor have spent years trying to keep their business out of Malaysia’s culture wars. A royal decree has dragged them straight into one.
The state’s decision to shut down pig farms, prompted by Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, Selangor’s hereditary ruler, has transformed a long-standing local dispute over pollution and odour into a flashpoint touching on royal influence, the livelihoods of a minority community and the delicate balancing act facing Malaysia’s multiracial government.

The row began last year as a local environmental complaint, with residents raising concerns over waste, smell, flies and river pollution from pig farms.

It escalated in January, when the Selangor palace objected to a state plan allowing pig farms in Tanjong Sepat, a coastal town in Kuala Langat district, to operate temporarily before moving to a centralised modern site in Bukit Tagar. The palace said problems linked to pig farming in Kuala Langat had not been resolved since 2010 and later made clear that Sultan Sharafuddin did not consent to pig farming anywhere in Selangor. Following the decree, the Selangor government stopped issuing new pig-farming licences and said existing farms would be closed in stages, with the state moving towards full imports of pork, local media reported.

Selangor, Malaysia’s richest state and the industrial belt around Kuala Lumpur, is governed by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s Pakatan Harapan coalition. Its multiracial image rests heavily on the Democratic Action Party (DAP), a Chinese-majority party often targeted by Malay-Muslim opponents.
Local media reported that former DAP assemblyman Ronnie Liu questioned why authorities were not looking at modern pig-farming systems and better waste treatment instead of closure.

That intervention ignited a political backlash. Critics accused Liu of derhaka, or disloyalty to the ruler, a loaded term in Malaysia, where criticism of the Malay rulers can quickly become a test of political loyalty rather than a debate over public policy.

Azmil Tayeb, a political scientist at Universiti Sains Malaysia, said the dispute was easily turned into a communal issue because pigs carried a religious and cultural stigma among Muslims.

“The issue is easily exploited because it evokes the image of dirtiness and unholiness among Muslims,” Azmil told This Week in Asia. “It means the issue is driven by sentiment, not by rational and clear-headed thinking.”

Malaysia is a parliamentary democracy, but its nine hereditary Malay rulers retain influence that goes far beyond ceremony, especially when an issue touches religion, Malay rights or public morality.

Former Malaysian Bar president Salim Bashir said it would be wrong to treat the sultan’s position as interference, especially with public welfare involved. “When a ruler provides advice on pig farming, floods or any other issues affecting the interest of the public, which later crystallises into a state policy, the decree is not to be treated as executive intrusion,” Salim said. “It is a reflection of His Majesty’s responsibilities to the state and people.”

AKTA PERSARAAN ANGGOTA PENTADBIRAN DAN AHLI PARLIMEN 2026

Suatu Akta untuk memansuhkan Akta Ahli Parlimen (Saraan) 1980 [Akta 237] secara berperingkat; untuk memperuntukkan pertukaran sistem persaraan bagi Anggota Pentadbiran dan Ahli Parlimen daripada Skim Pencen Tradisional kepada Skim Caruman Ditakrifkan (Defined Contribution Scheme); untuk mengawal selia hak persaraan sedia ada secara retrospektif; dan bagi perkara-perkara yang berkaitan dengannya.

BAHAGIAN I: PERMULAAN

1. Tajuk Ringkas dan Mula Berkuat Kuasa

(1) Akta ini bolehlah dinamakan Akta Reformasi Persaraan Anggota Pentadbiran dan Ahli Parlimen 2026.

(2) Akta ini hendaklah mula berkuat kuasa pada tarikh yang ditetapkan oleh Yang di-Pertuan Agong melalui pemberitahuan dalam Warta. (Selepas ini dirujuk sebagai "Tarikh Kuat Kuasa").

2. Tafsiran

Dalam Akta ini:

"Anggota Pentadbiran" membawa maksud menteri, timbalan menteri, menteri besar, ketua menteri, premier, dan ahli Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri (EXCO).

"Ahli Parlimen" dan "ADUN" merangkumi mana-mana individu yang dipilih melalui pilihan raya atau dilantik mengikut undang-undang ke dalam Dewan Rakyat, Dewan Negara, atau Dewan Undangan Negeri.

"Lantikan Politik" ertinya mana-mana individu yang dilantik oleh Kerajaan untuk memegang jawatan di dalam agensi kerajaan, badan berkanun, atau syarikat berkaitan kerajaan (GLC) atas kapasiti politik dan bukan melalui skim perkhidmatan awam biasa.

BAHAGIAN II: PEMANSUHAN DAN TRANSISI SKIM PERSARAAN

3. Pemansuhan Skim Pencen bagi Keahlian Baharu

(1) Mana-mana individu yang dipilih atau dilantik buat kali pertama sebagai Ahli Parlimen, ADUN, atau Anggota Pentadbiran pada atau selepas Tarikh Kuat Kuasa, individu tersebut tidak lagi layak di bawah skim pencen tradisional seumur hidup.

(2) Semua lantikan politik pada atau selepas Tarikh Kuat Kuasa hendaklah dibuat berasaskan sistem kontrak tanpa hak pencen atau ganjaran bulanan seumur hidup.

4. Penguatkuasaan Skim Caruman Baharu (KWSP/Sistem Setara)

(1) Setiap Ahli Parlimen, ADUN, Anggota Pentadbiran, dan Lantikan Politik yang tertakluk di bawah Seksyen 3 hendaklah didaftarkan sebagai pencarum di bawah Akta Kumpulan Wang Simpanan Pekerja 1991 [Akta 452].

(2) Kadar caruman hendaklah ditetapkan seperti berikut:

Caruman Syer Pekerja (Ahli Politik): 11% (atau kadar semasa) daripada elaun pokok bulanan.

Caruman Syer Majikan (Kerajaan): Seumpama kadar sektor awam atau swasta (contohnya 12%–13%).

BAHAGIAN III: KEDUDUKAN AHLI POLITIK VETERAN (VINTAJ LAMA)

5. Perlindungan Hak Retrospektif (Hak Masa Lalu)

(1) Tertakluk kepada Perkara 147 Perlembagaan Persekutuan, mana-mana individu yang telah melayakkan diri untuk menerima pencen di bawah Akta 237 sebelum Tarikh Kuat Kuasa, hak pencen mereka bagi tempoh perkhidmatan tersebut adalah dilindungi dan kekal sah.

(2) Pengiraan kadar pencen bagi perkhidmatan sebelum Tarikh Kuat Kuasa hendaklah dikunci (frozen) berdasarkan gaji pokok terakhir dan jumlah bulan perkhidmatan genap pada tarikh akta ini dikuatkuasakan.

6. Formula Hibrid bagi Ahli Politik Lama yang Menang Semula

(1) Jika seorang ahli politik veteran yang mempunyai rekod berkhidmat sebelum Tarikh Kuat Kuasa dipilih atau dilantik semula selepas Tarikh Kuat Kuasa:

(a) Perkhidmatan fasa baharu mereka hendaklah dicarumkan di bawah Skim KWSP mengikut Seksyen 4.

(b) Perkhidmatan fasa baharu tersebut tidak akan dikira untuk menambah sebarang peratusan gandaan (multiplier) atau menaikkan jumlah pencen lama di bawah Seksyen 5.

Gw selama ini mikir itu cuma "template bioskop" karena kebanyakan gitu. Ternyata pas gw bongkar lapkeu XXI, ini bukan sekedar iseng, tapi hasil desain yang strategis.

Sepanjang 2025, XXI (kode saham CNMA) cetak pendapatan sekitar Rp5,86 triliun. Dari situ, tiket nyumbang Rp3,6 triliun, dan makanan-minuman Rp2 triliun.
Coba resapi. Dari lima koma sekian triliun, dua triliunnya dari popcorn, soda, sama air botolan tadi.

Pasti ada yang nanya: kenapa nggak naikin harga tiket aja kalau mau cuan? Kenapa harus lewat snack?
Jawabannya ada di satu hal yang jarang dipikirin penonton. Tiket bioskop itu bukan sepenuhnya punya bioskop. Di model global, studio film ngambil potongan gede dari penjualan tiket, apalagi di minggu-minggu awal rilis. Angkanya bisa 60-70% lari ke studio (ini pola di pasar US, gw belum nemu rincian kontrak XXI yang dipublish).
Jadi dari tiket Rp50 ribu, yang nyangkut di kantong bioskop tipis.

Nah, makanan dan minuman beda cerita. Itu 100% punya bioskop, nggak dibagi ke siapa pun.
Dan marginnya brutal. Di chain gede kayak AMC sama Cinemark, margin F&B tembus 80 persenan. Popcorn yang modal bikinnya recehan bisa dijual dengan markup ratusan persen.

Ini namanya model "razor and blades". Sama kayak Xbox yang dijual rugi biar lo beli gamenya. Atau printer murah tapi tintanya mahal selangit.
Tiket itu umpan. Yang lo bayar pas haus dan laper di dalem, itu mesin duitnya.

Detik ketika lo masuk bioskop itu otomatis jadi captive audience. Nggak ada Indomaret di bioskop, nggak ada warung. Cuma ada satu penjual, dan dia yang nentuin harga. Air 22 ribu jadi masuk akal buat mereka, bukan buat lu.

Dan di Indonesia, XXI punya posisi industri bioskop yang bikin model ini makin kuat. Pas IPO 2023 mereka punya sekitar 225 bioskop, jauh di atas CGV (71) sama Cinepolis (60). Akhir 2025 udah 267 bioskop dan 1.388 layar.

Sebagian bisnis mencoba bertahan lewat digital marketing, kolaborasi influencer, dan program loyalitas yang bisa dongkrak omzet sampai 40%.

Tapi tanpa kebijakan sewa yang adil dan solusi tenaga kerja, sektor F&B Singapura tetap berada di ujung tanduk.
